key_insight: Photovoltaics can look highly favorable at the panel level, but once grid delivery, storage, backup, and fuel supply are included, the net energy advantage drops sharply and can become marginal for firm power.
engineering_relevance: For power-system designers, the paper shows that reliable decarbonization depends not just on adding renewables, but on preserving enough net-energy surplus after firming and infrastructure losses.
method: Expands the system boundary from installation-level EROI to reliable electricity supply
Compares wind-PV mix with battery, hydrogen, and gas-firmed configurations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark EROI ranges and lifecycle GWP$_{100}$ intensities across firming options, with no simulation or optimization of a real grid.
watch_item: Results are illustrative benchmarks with unity assumptions for orientation, site, curtailment, and delivery, so real-world deployment will likely have lower EROI and higher emissions.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
